hints: Split the phrase into its two parts. Ask yourself what makes immunity natural rather than artificial, and what makes it active rather than passive for these four methods.
Remember active means YOUR body meets the antigen and makes its own antibodies and memory cells, while natural means it happens by normal life exposure with no injection or medical help.
walkthrough:
**Decode the Two Key Words**

Hi there, let us break this down together. Natural means no human medical intervention, it just happens in everyday life.

Active means your own immune system does the work after meeting the antigen.

**Apply the Test to Each Method**

For active immunity, you must be exposed to the pathogen or its antigen, then you make your own antibodies and memory cells. This gives long lasting protection but takes time.

For passive immunity, you are simply GIVEN ready made antibodies from someone else, so it is fast but short lived and you make no memory cells.

**Pick the Natural Active Example**

Inhaling chicken pox virus in the air is a normal, natural exposure to the live pathogen. Your B lymphocytes then activate, make your own antibodies and memory cells, so this is natural active immunity.

options.A: This is natural passive immunity, because ready made antibodies in colostrum (first breast milk) are passed naturally from mother to baby.
options.B: This is natural active immunity, because you naturally catch the live virus and your own immune system makes antibodies and memory cells.
options.C: This is artificial passive immunity, because ready made antibodies are injected by a doctor and you make no memory cells yourself.
options.D: This is natural passive immunity, because ready made IgG antibodies cross the placenta naturally from mother to fetus.
